title: Procedure Pay Gap Explorer
lede: What Medicare assigns to matched procedures on female and male anatomy, from the public 2026 physician fee schedule. Pairs from the published literature are marked as such; the rest are Herada's own proposals, listed so they can be checked, not because they have been.
status: Draft. Held back until the pair review against Penn et al. (2025) and a clinician's check are done.

groups.same: One operation, two codes: the CPT code itself names the sex. The cleanest comparison there is, because the specialty, the setting and the operation are the same.
groups.published: Pairs from Goff, Muntz and Cain (1997), as re-used by Polan and Barber (2021). Matched for anatomic and technical similarity by the original authors.
groups.proposed: Herada's own anatomically matched pairs, not yet reviewed by a clinician. Each carries a match strength and the reason for it.
groups.popular: A comparison that circulates widely but is not a fair pair. Shown with its numbers so the mismatch is visible.

pairs.label: Total urethrectomy

female.plain: Removal of the entire urethra, female, with cystostomy

male.plain: Removal of the entire urethra, male, with cystostomy

pairs.note: Identical descriptor apart from the sex. Both sit in the urology chapter.

pairs.label: Excision of a urethral diverticulum

female.plain: Removal of a urethral diverticulum, female

male.plain: Removal of a urethral diverticulum, male

pairs.note: Identical descriptor apart from the sex.

pairs.label: Dilation of a urethral stricture, first visit

female.plain: Dilation of the female urethra, initial, including suppository or instillation

male.plain: Dilation of a urethral stricture by sound or dilator, male, initial

pairs.note: Office procedures with no global period. The female descriptor bundles a suppository or instillation; the male one names a stricture.

pairs.label: One-stage reconstruction of the urethra

female.plain: Reconstruction of the female urethra

male.plain: One-stage reconstruction of the male anterior urethra

pairs.note: Same chapter, same global period. The male code is limited to the anterior urethra.

pairs.label: Sling operation for stress incontinence

female.plain: Sling operation for stress urinary incontinence, female (fascia or synthetic)

male.plain: Sling operation for male urinary incontinence (fascia or synthetic)

pairs.note: Same operation and indication. The female code lives in the vagina chapter, the male code in the urethra chapter, so the two were valued separately.

pairs.label: Draining a deep abscess

female.plain: Incision and drainage of a vulvar or perineal abscess

male.plain: Incision and drainage of a deep abscess of the penis

pairs.label: Removing fluid-filled sacs

female.plain: Removal of ovarian cyst(s), one or both sides

male.plain: Removal of hydroceles, both sides

pairs.note: The ovarian procedure is intra-abdominal; the hydrocele repair is scrotal. The original authors still paired them.

pairs.label: Reconstructing the perineum or scrotum

female.plain: Perineoplasty, non-obstetric repair of the perineum

male.plain: Scrotoplasty, simple and complicated, averaged as the published analysis did

pairs.note: Global periods differ: 10 days for the perineoplasty, 90 for the scrotoplasties.

pairs.label: Removing the penis or the vagina

female.plain: Vaginectomy, complete removal of the vaginal wall

male.plain: Amputation of the penis, complete

pairs.label: Removing part of the vulva or the scrotum

female.plain: Simple partial vulvectomy

male.plain: Resection of the scrotum

pairs.label: Radical removal with groin lymph nodes

female.plain: Radical complete vulvectomy with groin lymph node removal on both sides

male.plain: Radical penectomy with groin lymph node removal

pairs.label: Radical removal with groin and pelvic lymph nodes

female.plain: Radical complete vulvectomy with groin and pelvic lymph node removal

male.plain: Radical penectomy with groin and pelvic lymph node removal

pairs.label: Removing the cervix or part of the prostate

female.plain: Trachelectomy, removal of the cervix

male.plain: Subtotal prostatectomy, suprapubic

pairs.note: The loosest of the published pairs anatomically; kept because it is in the published set.

pairs.label: Cancer surgery with limited lymph node sampling

female.plain: Total abdominal hysterectomy with pelvic and para-aortic node sampling, tubes and ovaries optional

male.plain: Radical retropubic prostatectomy with limited pelvic lymph node removal

pairs.label: Radical cancer surgery with full pelvic lymph node removal

female.plain: Radical abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy and para-aortic node sampling

male.plain: Radical retropubic prostatectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy

pairs.label: Radical cancer surgery through the perineum or the vagina

female.plain: Radical vaginal hysterectomy

male.plain: Radical perineal prostatectomy

pairs.label: Pelvic exenteration for cancer

female.plain: Pelvic exenteration for gynecologic cancer

male.plain: Pelvic exenteration for bladder, prostate or urethral cancer

pairs.note: The male-side code covers bladder and urethral cancer in anyone; the published analysis treated it as the prostate-cancer pair.

pairs.label: Biopsy of the external genitals

female.plain: Biopsy of the vulva or perineum, one lesion

male.plain: Biopsy of the penis

pairs.note: Both are office biopsies with no global period.

pairs.label: Destroying lesions such as warts, simple

female.plain: Destruction of vulvar lesions, simple, any method

male.plain: Destruction of penile lesions, simple, chemical

pairs.note: The vulvar code covers any method; the penile codes are split by method, and the chemical one is used here.

pairs.label: Destroying lesions such as warts, extensive

female.plain: Destruction of vulvar lesions, extensive, any method

male.plain: Destruction of penile lesions, extensive, any method

pairs.label: Biopsy of the ovary or the testis

female.plain: Biopsy of the ovary, one or both sides

male.plain: Biopsy of the testis, incisional

pairs.note: The ovarian biopsy is an abdominal operation with a 90-day global; the testicular biopsy is a scrotal incision with a 10-day global.

pairs.label: Removing the ovary or the testis, open

female.plain: Oophorectomy, partial or total, one or both sides

male.plain: Simple orchiectomy, with or without a prosthesis

pairs.note: Polan and Barber named this as a pair worth studying that their data could not cover.

pairs.label: Removing the ovary or the testis, laparoscopic

female.plain: Laparoscopic removal of the ovary and/or tube

male.plain: Laparoscopic orchiectomy

pairs.note: Global periods differ: 10 days for the female code, 90 for the male one.

pairs.label: Removing the fallopian tube or the epididymis

female.plain: Salpingectomy, complete or partial, one or both sides

male.plain: Epididymectomy

pairs.note: Analogous structures, different approaches: abdominal versus scrotal.

pairs.label: Reversing a sterilization

female.plain: Tubotubal anastomosis, rejoining the fallopian tubes

male.plain: Vasovasostomy, rejoining the vas deferens

pairs.note: Both are microsurgical re-anastomoses of a duct.

pairs.label: Biopsy of the uterine lining or the prostate

female.plain: Endometrial biopsy, without cervical dilation

male.plain: Prostate biopsy, any approach, without imaging guidance

pairs.note: Both are office sampling procedures with no global period, but the techniques differ: a suction catheter versus needle cores. CPT 2026 split the old single prostate-biopsy code into five by approach; the non-imaging one is used here, and the image-guided codes (55707 to 55709) carry more work.

pairs.label: Sterilization: tubal ligation vs. vasectomy

female.plain: Laparoscopic tubal sterilization by fulguration

male.plain: Vasectomy, one or both sides

pairs.note: Not a fair pair. A vasectomy is an office procedure under local anesthetic; laparoscopic sterilization is an operating-room procedure under general anesthesia. The gap here reflects the operation, not the sex.

literature.authors: Goff BA, Muntz HG, Cain JM
literature.title: Comparison of 1997 Medicare relative value units for gender-specific procedures: is Adam still worth more than Eve?
literature.finding: 24 matched pairs, 1997 values. The male-specific procedure carried the higher work RVU in 19 (80%) and the higher total RVU in 20 (83%); work RVUs averaged 49% higher and reimbursement 37% higher for the male-specific procedure.

literature.authors: Benoit MF, Ma JF, Upperman BA
literature.title: Comparison of 2015 Medicare relative value units for gender-specific procedures: gynecologic and gynecologic-oncologic versus urologic CPT coding. Has time healed gender-worth?
literature.finding: 50 matched pairs, 2015 values. The male-specific procedure carried higher work and total RVUs in 36 (72%) and a higher fee in 42 (84%); male-specific surgeries averaged 27.67% higher reimbursement.

literature.title: Reimbursement for female-specific compared with male-specific procedures over time
literature.finding: 12 of the 1997 pairs, with operating times from the NSQIP registry. The male-specific procedure carried the higher RVU in 9 of 12 pairs in 1997 and 6 of 12 in 2015. Per hour of operating, female-specific procedures earned more RVUs (10.6 vs 9.7) but fewer dollars ($555 vs $599), because specialties are paid different amounts per RVU.

literature.authors: Penn M, Colley D, Koirala P, King L, Fitzgerald J
literature.title: Price and prejudice: reimbursement of surgical care on male versus female anatomies
literature.finding: 55 anatomically matched procedures (110 CPT codes), 2023 values, pairs verified by gynecologists and urologists. The female-anatomy procedure had the lower RVU in 41 (75%); male-anatomy RVUs averaged 30% higher; facility reimbursement was higher for the male procedure in 35 (64%), by 25.6% on average. Across 2003 to 2023 the average male advantage stayed at 31 to 34%.
